biggest_gap.what: The bloodstain the whole piece exists to walk back to is not drawn from most approach bearings. RI-JRN06 M-D14 requires it visible at 12 m in daylight and 6 m in the dark; the aggregation measures 1 of 8 bearings and 3 of 8 respectively, with the bloom frame pixel-identical (195 px) to the in-row 180-degree-away control at every failing bearing. The bloom holds 4,200 souls at [3834.57,2.97,3959.5]. Round 1 could not see it because it shot one bearing; the round-2 CONSUMPTION artifact could not see it because it used bloom_px:195 as its RECOVERED-state null control — the same 195 this check reads as 'nothing rendered'.
biggest_gap.why_this_one: Everything else the piece protects is bookkeeping that holds — conservation exact, one stain, nothing softened, no fast travel to the corpse — and all of it exists to make ONE WALK matter. There is no light on the floor from most directions.
biggest_gap.remedy: Make the bloom a camera-facing billboard with a vertical emissive component, or raise its origin above the local ground normal, in render/renderer.js syncDeathMarkers(). It is currently either single-sided, sunk into the heightfield, or occluded by marsh reed instancing at grazing angles.
biggest_gap.acceptance: m_d14_stain_visibility reports 8/8 daylight at 12 m and 8/8 dark at 6 m with the in-row 180-degree control still at its floor at every bearing, INSIDE a full journey-run.mjs --journey jrn06-death run rather than a standalone probe; and the same run's m_d8_second_death goes green.

secondary_observations.what: Souls now have a sink and on every session without sim.character the sink is a hole. Two arms, one browser, identical frames, spends driven through the real input path: arm no-character (the shipped 'default' state, which is what the ROUND-2 BUILDER'S OWN levelling probe used) spent 37,652 souls across 24 levels and moved hp_max 620->620, stamina_max 120->120, focus_max 94->94, leaving sim._poolsDirty stuck true forever; arm with-character moved hp_max 300->508, stamina_max 104->130, focus_max 30->56 for exactly the same spends. THE CONTROL GOES GREEN. Mechanism: Engine.applyDerivedPools() opens `const ch = this.sim.character; if (!ch) return null;`. Its own header comment describes this failure as already fixed once — 'VIGOUR 6 and VIGOUR 18 both reported hp_max 620'. VIGOUR 18 reports hp_max 620. So round 2's headline (souls 4,200 -> 3,782 = exactly soulsToNextLevel()) is true and is arithmetic: the money left and the character did not change.

The level-up screen offers ten attributes and the character has six, and they are different vocabularies. Read off the DRAWN elements: STRENGTH 12, ENDURANCE 20, AGILITY 10, SPEED 10, VIGOUR 10, WILLPOWER 10, INTELLECT 10, HIST-BOND 10, PERSONALITY 10, LUCK 10 — while the character carries vigour 10, endurance 20, strength 12, dexterity 12, intelligence 10, faith 10. Seven rows are for attributes the character does not have, each drawing a constant 10, and confirming one MINTS the key at 11 because _spendSouls does prog.attributes[attrId] = (prog.attributes[attrId] || 10) + 1 with no validation. Three of the character's real attributes (dexterity, intelligence, faith) are not on the screen and cannot be raised. The screen's own preview for speed and agility reads derived: [] — it promises nothing. Across the whole build `speed` is named by no pool, no reaction, no faction gate and no quest requirement. TWO OF THE BUILDER'S OWN THREE HEADLINE SPENDS were agility (hearth-lilmoth) and speed (hearth-gideon), both recorded pass:true with souls_matches_cost:true.

Respawn drift 0.00 m at 6 of 6 is the MEASUREMENT, not the fix. Four arms per well in one run: released 0.00 m; held 9.78 m (archon) / 13.97 m (stormhold) / 12.86 m (gideon) at 220 frames, 1.57-2.24 m off the basin on the respawn frame itself; released with traversal.reset() stubbed out 0.00 m; HELD with traversal.reset() stubbed out 9.78 m and 13.97 m — IDENTICAL TO THE DIGIT. The line _afterRespawnPlacement() added is inert: with the axis released there is no velocity to reset, with it held the body re-accelerates on the next frame anyway. Round 1's finding stands unfixed — a player killed while running is 8-14 m from the basin 3.7 s later without touching the controller — and RI-PRG04 D6's 'they are standing at the HEARTH' is still true for one frame.

It is four purses, not two, and the one the player reads is a hard zero. The inventory screen's drawn `inventory.gold` element reads '0 gold' at start, after setGold(777), after fencing, and after a save/load round trip — because engine.js reads (sim.loadout && sim.loadout.gold) || sim.gold || 0 and NEITHER sim.loadout NOR sim.gold is ever defined on the sim. Meanwhile progression.gold 0/777/777/777, stealth.p.gold 400 throughout (never touched by setGold), magic.gold 0/777/777/777, combat.world.gold 0/0/0/777. The builder was right to file the two-purse defect and it is one field bigger than filed. Not W1-13's model — W1-15/crime and W1-21/interface own it — but it is the mechanism behind the save critic's separately-reported defect.

journey-run.mjs really is handing jrn06 an open inventory screen, and the builder's gate caught it live: m_jrn06_entry_screen_closed reports ui_mode_on_entry 'inventory', ui_mode_after_close 'world', advanced 5. Without it this aggregation would have been twenty fictional rows. But the SAME open screen breaks journey-run.mjs's own pre-legs one step earlier and those are unguarded: control_observed is unmeasurable ('the player did not move between [2766.5,2.68,5011] and [2766.5,2.68,5011] after 60 frames of forward input'), taking first_control and m4_clause1 with it. Swept: 12 of 12 combinations of {arena_flat, settlement_primary_street, barge-hold} x {inventory, journal, sheet, map} freeze the world and loadState rescues none of them. Only jrn06-death.mjs carries a gate; jrn01/02/03/05/07/08/09 are all exposed.

Two aggregate counts are still properties of the harness rather than of the build. m_d10_death_legibility n 20 max_frames 0 — all twenty deaths are damagePlayer(1e5), so 'HP reaches 0 within 12 frames of the last hit' measures the verb. m_d2_stain_placement placement_rules {death_point: 20}, max_offset_m 0, mean_offset_m 0 — the fall / last-grounded / drown / fog-gate rules the builder fixed and demonstrated standalone do not fire ONCE in twenty journey deaths, so round 1's '0.000 m describes the probe' is completely unmoved by the aggregation. The fixes are real (placement.json shows the fall rule anchoring 0.00 m from the ledge and 63.64 m from the floor); the journey cannot reach them.

A failing check still reaches the ledger as ok. jrn06-death.mjs's put() calls led.ok() unconditionally and only ADDS a separate log('FAIL ...') line, so both failing checks appear in the ledger dump as '[OK ] m_d8_second_death ...' and '[OK ] m_d14_stain_visibility ...'. journey.ok is false and the FAIL lines are printed, so nothing is concealed — but the per-check surface a human reads says OK for a check that failed.

M-D5's third documented world-side writer has no user. respawn.json documents three producers of the six never-respawn flags. Statblock is real (champion_hist_marked and cst_sap_speaker both declare boss+unique, though redundantly with never_respawn_ids). World map is real and I re-derived it (below). But the caller/state-file route — engine.js:661-667 carrying the six flags out of a named state's `spawn:` block — has ZERO users: game/data/states/*.json declares 18 spawn entries and none of them carries any of the six. 'A quest can place a named actor in DATA' is still paperwork.

path_to_ten: Draw the bloom. M-D14 8/8 daylight at 12 m and 8/8 dark at 6 m inside a full journey run, with the 180-degree-away control still at its floor. (the named gap)
Place a stain on a second death, or file the arbitration question against RI-JRN06 M-D8's 'always'. m_d8_second_death goes green in the aggregate either way.

Make a level buy something: derive the pools from progression.attributes unconditionally and apply birthsign terms only when sim.character exists. Acceptance: probe-b's no-character arm reports the same hp_max/stamina_max/focus_max deltas as its with-character arm, and sim._poolsDirty returns to false after every spend.

Make the level-up screen list the character's attributes: zero rows for an attribute the character does not carry, zero carried attributes missing from the screen, and _spendSouls refuses an id outside the declared set instead of minting it.

Give the drift a real answer: either clear the held move axis across a death or state that carrying momentum through a respawn is intended. Acceptance: a drift measurement with the axis HELD, at six wells, against a stated target.

Gate the other journeys: lift jrn06-death.mjs's WORLD-RUNS-ON-ENTRY block into journey-run.mjs so it runs once before every journey, and fix whichever leg leaves the inventory screen open. control_observed should be measured, not unmeasurable.
Make M-D2 and M-D10 reachable: twenty damagePlayer deaths on flat standable ground cannot exercise four placement rules or a legibility window. Drive at least one death per rule inside the journey.

Give sim.loadout.gold a definition or point inventory.gold at the real purse — and pick one purse. Four is three too many and the screen reads none of them. (W1-15 / W1-21, filed here with the measurement.)
Clear the two corpus_debt items (RI-PRG04 M9, M10) and the M10 arbitration question.

self_audit.which: CONSUMPTION model 2b (fog gate boss -> respawn classification) re-derived by my own world-map perturbation; and the respawn-drift 0.00 m re-derived and shown to be an artefact of the released input rather than of the fix.
self_audit.how: probe-c sabotaged closeMenu() to a no-op that returns the mode it failed to close, and the gate went red (advanced 0, gate_would_refuse true) against a healthy control (advanced 5); probe-b's with-character arm moved every pool the no-character arm left flat; probe-d stubbed traversal.reset() in all four drift arms.

notes: Round 1 scored 4 and named a gap that is genuinely closed. Round 2 earned the increase to 5: the mid-death save is fixed across nine save moments, M-D7 was written from nothing and passes, M-D4 went from a stale volatile list to four seeds with a deliberate falsifiability control, the fall rule fires, the fog gate no longer degenerates at its centre, and the WORLD-RUNS-ON-ENTRY gate is the best instrument work in the piece — I tried to make it lie and it refused, and my own run proves it was needed. What the round did not do is look behind the door it opened.
